data.title: Agoda Reports Rise in International Travel Interest to Kaohsiung and Taipei During BTS and BIGBANG Concerts
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Oct. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Concerts are not only bringing fans to venues but are also increasingly becoming a reason for international travelers to plan a trip to Taiwan. With South Korean boy bands BIGBANG performing in Taipei in October and BTS heading to Kaohsiung in November, digital travel platform Agoda's latest search data shows growing international travel interest to Taiwan during these major K-pop concerts. Accommodation searches from international travelers to Kaohsiung during BTS' concert dates grew 3.6x compared to two weeks prior, while international searches to Taipei during BIGBANG's concert dates increased by 38% compared to two weeks prior, highlighting how concert travel can be a contributor to inbound travel interest to Taiwan.

Kaohsiung steps onto the stage as a world-class concert destination

Kaohsiung has been actively developing its concert economy in recent years — according to the city government, its concert economy has generated an estimated NT$18.9 billion in tourism output since 2023, including 157 concerts and 1.71 million attendees in 2024 alone. Major performances are also generating activity beyond concert venues and extending into accommodation, dining and tourism spending. According to an analysis by Taiwan's National Credit Card Center on concert-related spending in Kaohsiung between 2023 and 2025, international visitors accounted for 3.85% of attendees at concerts by international artists, compared with 2.20% for concerts by local artists. International visitors also spent an average of NT$8,772 per card on accommodation, approximately twice as much as domestic visitors.

It's no surprise that Kaohsiung is now a natural stop for some of the world's biggest tours, including BTS. The Kaohsiung National Stadium is reported to be fully booked for all of 2026, and its metro reached 350,000 riders in a single day during last November's TWICE concerts, according to Mayor Chen Chi-mai, showcasing how well-equipped the city is to handle crowds of this scale. BTS WORLD TOUR 'ARIRANG' will take place at Kaohsiung National Stadium on November 19, 21 and 22, giving international fans another reason to plan a longer stay in southern Taiwan.

Japanese travelers show the strongest appetite for concert travel to Taiwan

Looking more closely at source markets, Japanese travelers showed the strongest growth in travel interest around both concert dates. Accommodation searches from Japanese travelers to Taipei during the BIGBANG concert dates were over 6x higher than the two weeks prior, while searches to Kaohsiung during the BTS concert dates were even higher at more than 14x, highlighting the appeal of major K-pop performances in Taiwan among travelers from nearby Japan.

Travel interest to Kaohsiung during the BTS concert dates also extended beyond Japan. According to Agoda, the Philippines emerged as the top travelers searching for accommodations in Kaohsiung during the concert dates, with a nearly 3x growth in searches compared to two weeks prior, followed by Japan (14.3x), Singapore (8.4x), Hong Kong (2.2x), and Thailand (1.9x).

For BIGBANG's Taipei concerts, the top five source markets that expressed travel interest were Japan, the Philippines (+19%), Thailand (+89%), South Korea (+30%), and Singapore (+29%). The increase in travel interest from multiple Asian markets suggests a strong opportunity for concerts to not only attract travelers to the event but also encourage international travelers to look beyond Taipei to explore southern Taiwan.

Jishan Chai, Country Director for Taiwan at Agoda, said: "The chance to see your favorite artists in concert is increasingly becoming an important reason for travelers to plan a trip. Our data shows that international fans are looking beyond Taipei, with more international performances taking place in Kaohsiung and generating travel interest from markets including Japan, Singapore and the Philippines. A concert can also be the starting point for exploring a city, giving fans an opportunity to turn their trip into a broader travel experience in Taiwan."

Agoda offers more than 6 million holiday properties, over 130,000 flight routes, and more than 300,000 activities, enabling travelers to conveniently plan accommodation, flights and experiences in one place. Travelers can discover more deals and travel options on the Agoda app or Agoda.com.

SOURCE Agoda

data.title: 'We Need to Win.' Inside the Five-Year Quest to Reinvent the Goldfish. — WSJ
data.description:
By Jesse Newman | Photography and Video by Cam McLeod for WSJ

Inside Campbell's headquarters this past March, executives stared at a problem: Their new gluten-free Goldfish crackers looked like sharks.

The smile was all wrong too. The specialty Goldfish had a menacing quality.

"It was more like if you've ever seen 'Jaws,'" says George Vindiola, who leads research and development at Campbell's. "Like the look of the great white shark."

Brian Hannigan, Campbell's head of innovation, told Vindiola's team to try again. Their first large-scale production run was unacceptable.

"This is probably not the Goldfish experience that we want to be giving to kids," Hannigan recalls thinking.

Gluten, it turned out, gives dough a springy, elastic quality. Once the dough is cut, regular Goldfish contract, snapping back into the classic, plump fish shape before baking. But the gluten-free dough, made without wheat, stayed stretched out.

Vindiola, who has worked for 30 years in R&D, agreed to try. He had figured out how to add white chocolate to Pepperidge Farm Milano cookies and put pepperoncini into Kettle Brand potato chips but this was tougher. He warned Hannigan there was no guarantee his team could fix the fish in time for their planned launch on grocery store shelves in November.

The difference between a cracker that smiles and one that doesn't seems tiny — roughly five mm, in fact. But for old-line food makers like Campbell's, getting any sales growth is so hard that gains can be measured in millimeters.

Campbell's, known for the red-and-white cans of soup that Andy Warhol turned into Pop art, faces particular challenges. Eating habits have changed. People aren't eating as much canned soups and packaged snacks, its two main businesses. Fresher foods and newer brands are where the growth is. The company is on track to post its fourth consecutive annual decline in comparable sales this year. Its stock has fallen 29% over the past year.

So the soup-and-snack maker is cutting costs. As part of its goal to eliminate $500 million in costs by fiscal 2030, Campbell's has cut more than 550 jobs, or roughly 13% of its salaried workforce. It closed its factory on Cape Cod in Massachusetts that makes Cape Cod potato chips. And it plans to slash its quarterly dividend to 25 cents a share, down 36% from its prior dividend of 39 cents a share.

Campbell's chief executive Mick Beekhuizen is also trying to update the company's core products. Goldfish is one of its four biggest brands, with $1 billion in annual sales. Campbell's snack sales have fallen for the past three fiscal years, on a comparable basis.

"With Goldfish, we need to grow, we need to win," Beekhuizen told investors in September.

Goldfish were the brainchild of Oscar Kambly, a Swiss baker who created the cracker in 1958 as a birthday gift for his wife — a Pisces — whose astrological sign was a fish.

Pepperidge Farm founder Margaret Rudkin discovered Goldfish while on vacation in Europe and in 1962 licensed the crackers to sell in the U.S., marketing them as a bar snack for adults. Campbell's had newly acquired Pepperidge Farm and began promoting Goldfish. Astronauts brought them to space aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery in 1988. About a decade later, Campbell's added a smiley face to many Goldfish varieties and the bar snack became a ubiquitous kids' snack.

Since then, Campbell's, based in Camden, NJ, has struggled to adapt to changing consumer tastes that have buffeted the food industry.

As sales of other products lagged, Goldfish was a bright spot. Demand was so strong that Campbell's in 2023 decided to invest $160 million to add a new production line at its Richmond, Utah, plant. The line, built to produce over five million Goldfish per hour, would increase the plant's Goldfish output by 50% percent. It marked the company's third capacity expansion for Goldfish in two years, Campbell's said at the time.

Goldfish buyers were evenly split between households with and without kids, says Janda Lukin, Campbell's chief growth officer. The Covid pandemic had closed schools and fewer snacks were being packed in lunchboxes or for after-school activities — so Campbell's decided to focus more on adults. The company debuted Goldfish Mega Bites, which are 50% bigger than the original, and new, limited-edition flavors like Frank's RedHot, Old Bay and Jalapeño Popper.

"It's come to our attention that some people think Goldfish crackers are just for kids," said a 2024 Goldfish ad online. "Well, what if we call them "Chilean Sea Bass?"

Campbell's that year forecast that Goldfish would reach $1.3 billion in sales by fiscal 2027.

The company's timing was poor. By the time the factory expansion was complete in 2024, Goldfish sales volumes had slowed, according to a BNP Paribas analysis of NIQ data. Declines have worsened recently, falling 5% versus year-ago levels in the four weeks ended Oct. 3, the data shows.

So Campbell's reversed course on Goldfish. In its March earnings call, CEO Beekhuizen said the company would once again focus on families with kids.

Campbell's introduced limited-edition Goldfish in the shape of four Pokémon characters in June. It decided to appeal to parents looking for healthier snacks that kids will eat with three new varieties — with added protein, whole grains and gluten-free. And it updated its packaging to highlight that Goldfish have long been made with 100% real cheese and no artificial colors or flavors.

Creating a gluten-free Goldfish has been the request it gets the most often, Campbell's says.

The company first tried five years ago to create a cracker that people who avoid gluten could eat, said Vindiola, the research and development head. But, in tests, the gluten-free cracker — made with a blend of rice flour, tapioca flour, cornstarch and potato starch instead of wheat — tasted bland. Campbell's also faced hurdles because it didn't have gluten-free plants or production lines so it couldn't prevent cross-contamination with wheat flour used in its other Goldfish.

The company decided to try again, calling the effort "Project Emma" after a 10-year-old girl named Emma Livingston who wrote to Campbell's last year asking for a gluten-free Goldfish for her sister with celiac disease.

"My sister is just one of the millions of kids that have celiac," Livingston wrote in her letter, a copy of which was reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. "If more people buy your product, you'd obviously make even more money than you do right now."

This time, Campbell's ran into problems with its dough. The gluten-free mixture was too sticky to pass through the rollers that flatten the dough into sheets. Employees tweaked the recipe, adjusting the amount and timing of the water they added and how long they mixed the dough.

The gluten-free Goldfish baked up nicely in Campbell's pilot.

But things went haywire when the company tried to produce the crackers at scale. To save time, Campbell's hired a third-party manufacturer to make the cracker, rather than retool its own facilities. The first run at that plant in March produced the sharks with an evil-looking grin.

"They weren't like a typical Goldfish that has a nice blunt nose and has the eyes and smiles," Vindiola says.

With the next and last run scheduled for May, Campbell's R&D team redesigned the cutter, adjusting its size and the depth and curve of the fish's smile. If their calculations were still off, the company could miss its window for a fall launch in grocery stores.

But the new cutters worked, producing Goldfish in their classic shape with their signature smile. Gluten-free Goldfish are slightly crispier than the traditional crackers, executives said, but otherwise the cheddar cheese and spice taste is the same. Campbell's convinced grocers to give it the retail Holy Grail — space on store shelves to sell gluten-free Goldfish alongside its regular varieties. The specialty crackers will go on sale in the coming weeks.

Beekhuizen told investors in September that sales of its core, cheddar Goldfish were improving, though they are still declining overall. The company recently launched a new marketing campaign, bringing back its old "Snack That Smiles Back" jingle, and is investing in more family-oriented options like multipacks.

"I'm encouraged by Goldfish, but we have much more work to do," Beekhuizen said.

  • Photography and Video assisting by Dylan Totaro

data.title: Abound Declares H2si Power Incorporated in Material Default of H2si™ License Agreement
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Richmond, BC – TheNewswire - October 30, 2026 - ABOUND Energy Inc. (“ABOUND” or the “Company”) (FSE: 0E9) announces that it has declared H2Si Power Incorporated (“H2Si”), Amerada R&D Ltd. (“Amerada”) and Robert McKenzie in material default of the H2Si Technology Commercialization and License Agreement dated June 27, 2026 (the “License Agreement”) and the related support and guarantee agreement (the “Guarantee Agreement”). Among other things, the Company alleges that H2Si failed to deliver the technical drawings required to build the first commercial unit (the “FCU”), and that Mr. McKenzie concealed from the Company that he has been marketing, through another company, SiFusion Energy Inc. (“SiFusion”), technology that the Company believes is the H2Si™ technology for which it holds an exclusive license.

    Background

    As announced on May 7, June 30 and July 31, 2026, ABOUND obtained exclusive commercialization and licensing rights to the H2Si™ hydrogen technology (the “H2Si Technology”) under the License Agreement, which closed on July 31, 2026. As consideration, the Company issued 5,000,000 common shares to H2Si, of which 1,000,000 were delivered at closing and 4,000,000 are held in escrow under a pooling and escrow agreement, to be released only if the FCU meets specified performance criteria. Under the Guarantee Agreement, Amerada and Mr. McKenzie guaranteed the performance of all of H2Si’s obligations under the License Agreement, as to 30% and 70% respectively, up to an aggregate of US$5,000,000, and Amerada agreed not to directly or indirectly support any alternative licence or disposition of the H2Si Technology. Mr. McKenzie is the President of H2Si and the sole director of Amerada.

    Material Default

    On September 21, 2026, the Company delivered a notice of material default (the “Notice”) to H2Si, Amerada and Mr. McKenzie. The Company alleges, among other things, that:

    (a)        Mr. McKenzie, through H2Si, failed to deliver the technical drawings and specifications required under the License Agreement to build the FCU, despite repeated assurances that they existed, and H2Si’s counsel has since confirmed that the technical drawings and specifications for the H2Si Technology do not exist;

    (b)        H2Si, Amerada and Mr. McKenzie concealed from the Company that Mr. McKenzie, as President and Chief Executive Officer of SiFusion, has been marketing technology the Company believes to be the H2Si Technology, or derived from it, through SiFusion and other entities. SiFusion’s website describes the technology as held under exclusive license from the inventor, refers to the same University of Saskatchewan testing previously announced by the Company, and describes SiFusion as affiliated with the Amerada group of companies. The Company alleges that this conduct breaches Amerada’s covenant under the Guarantee Agreement not to support any alternative licence of the H2Si Technology;

    (c)        H2Si has failed to enforce and protect its intellectual property in the H2Si Technology, as required under the License Agreement, by failing to take any action against Mr. McKenzie or SiFusion. Instead, Mr. McKenzie purportedly moved to remove two H2Si directors who were working on behalf of H2Si to cure the defaults. Both directors have since resigned, leaving Mr. McKenzie and Gary Woycenko as the remaining directors of H2Si; and

    (d)        H2Si and Mr. McKenzie have failed to cooperate with the Company to remedy the defaults.

    The Company has also notified Amerada and Mr. McKenzie that this conduct falls within the obligations they guaranteed under the Guarantee Agreement and has delivered a cease and desist demand to SiFusion.

    Failure to Remedy to Date

    Since closing of the License Agreement, the Company received numerous assurances from H2Si counsel that the required technical drawings and specifications would be provided and that a formal response would be forthcoming. Despite these assurances, the latest response the Company has received is an unsigned letter from Mr. McKenzie dated September 22, 2026, and received on September 29, 2026, purportedly on behalf of H2Si, Amerada, and Mr. McKenzie, which disputed the Notice without remedying the defaults or providing the requested information. Furthermore, Mr. McKenzie has refused to meet with the Company since August 13, 2026, failed to engage following delivery of the Notice, and failed to provide a valid address for formal service. H2Si has demonstrated a persistent failure to remedy or take meaningful steps toward compliance.

    Two H2Si directors had been working with the Company to cure the defaults and were the Company’s principal contacts at H2Si. After Mr. McKenzie purportedly moved to remove them, both directors resigned. Their departure removes the channel through which the Company had been working toward a resolution and leaves H2Si’s counsel and its two remaining directors, Mr. McKenzie and Mr. Woycenko, as the Company’s only contacts at H2Si. The Company has concluded that these matters are unlikely to be resolved cooperatively and is taking further steps to protect its rights. These developments may affect the commercialization of the H2Si Technology under the Company’s exclusive license, the shares issued to H2Si, and the timing of the FCU.

    “ABOUND entered into this transaction in good faith and secured exclusive rights to the H2Si Technology for the benefit of our shareholders,” said Keith Morlock, Chief Operating Officer. “We have worked patiently to resolve these matters directly, but recent events have made it clear that more is required. We remain committed to building the first commercial unit, and we will take every step necessary to protect our rights.”

    Next Steps

    The Company remains committed to completing the FCU, and the steps it is taking are directed toward that objective. The Company has not terminated the License Agreement and is evaluating all remedies available to it, including proceedings against H2Si and claims against Amerada and Mr. McKenzie under the Guarantee Agreement. The escrowed shares will not be released unless the FCU achieves the specified performance criteria, and the Company has asked its transfer agent to place a hold on all shares issued to H2Si. The Company’s allegations have not been tested in any proceeding. The matters described in this news release are not exhaustive. Additional claims may arise as the Company continues its review, and nothing in this news release limits or waives any of the Company’s rights, claims or remedies, all of which are expressly reserved.

    About ABOUND Energy Inc.

    ABOUND Energy Inc. is a clean-energy technology commercialization company building a diversified Energy Solutions Platform across ZaeroTex™ advanced air cathodes, H2Si™ hydrogen technology and Zaeras™ long-duration energy storage.

    Keith Morlock, Chief Operating Officer

    Email: Investors@Abound.Energy

    Ph: +1 604-822-9082

    Forward-Looking Information

    This news release contains forward-looking information within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities laws, including statements regarding the Notice, the cure period under the License Agreement, the Company’s rights and remedies and any proceedings it may commence, the release of the escrowed shares and the hold on the shares issued to H2Si, and the Company’s plans to complete the FCU. Forward-looking information is based on assumptions management considers reasonable, including that the Company’s rights under the License Agreement and the Guarantee Agreement will be upheld, that the transfer agent will maintain the hold on the shares issued to H2Si, and that the technical information required to build the FCU can be obtained or developed. It is subject to risks that may cause actual results to differ materially, including that the Company’s allegations may not be upheld, the outcome of any dispute or proceedings with H2Si, Amerada, Mr. McKenzie or SiFusion, the costs and timing of enforcing the Company’s rights, the ability to recover amounts under the Guarantee Agreement, delays in or the inability to complete the FCU, and the potential loss of the Company’s rights to the H2Si Technology. Readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on forward-looking information. Except as required by applicable securities laws, the Company undertakes no obligation to update it.
